en: Soldier: Victory to the Great King! King:
Water, first.
Attendant: As the Great King commands. (Exiting and re-entering) Here is the water.
The King: Arjuna! Let Uttara be accepted as the bride-price for the victory in the seizure of the cattle.
The Blessed One: [Silent]
This head is bowed down.
Arjuna:
How does he compare my conduct? O King!
The entire beloved inner apartment has been honored by me like a mother;
this daughter of Uttara is now being accepted by you for the sake of a son. (71)
The Blessed One:
This head is held high. The King: [It is so.]
Now, established in the conduct of those who are heroes in battle,
he has performed an action befitting a resident of the inner apartments.
"Truly, today is an auspicious constellation; let his marriage take place this very day.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: "So be it, so be it. Let us send a reply to our grandfather."
The King: Whatever pleases you. O Dharmarāja, Vṛkodara, and Dhanañjaya! This way, this way, sirs! Let us enter the inner apartments with this very joy.
All: [They do so.]
Very well.
(All exit.
The third act.
Then enters a soldier. Soldier: Ho there! Let it be announced, let it be announced to all the Kṣatriyas, headed by the preceptors of the entire warrior class: for this—
Having cast aside the fear born of Nārāyaṇa’s discus and having treated the Pāṇḍavas— who have long since perished— as mere contemptibles,
he was not protected by the Kurus, even with their bows as allies.
Abhimanyu has been carried off; let shame be cast aside!
Thus (then enter Bhīṣma and Droṇa). Droṇa:
O charioteer! Speak, speak!
By whom has this disciple’s son, skilled in battle, been brought before me? Who here desires to fight with my arrows, as if with the gods themselves?
Declare the excellence of that man, as well as his weapons or his strength, so that I may dispatch messengers with arrows to him.
Bhīṣma:
O charioteer! Speak, speak!
He is delayed by the impulses of youth, his fault being his ignorance regarding the necessity of retreat when broken.
"By whom was this young elephant seized as the herd departed, while he was intent on grasping a tusker? || 3 ||
(Then Duryodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni enter. Duryodhana: Charioteer! Tell me, tell me! By whom has Abhimanyu been carried away? I myself shall set him free. Why so?
For my fathers initiated this division among kinsmen; therefore, the fault for this must be cast upon me by those who speak of it.
Moreover, that son of mine [was born] after the Pāṇḍavas.
And when there is a conflict within a family, children do not commit an offense. || 4 ||
Karṇa:
Mother Gāndhārī, you have spoken with great affection and what is fitting.
Let it not be that, out of childishness and thinking him to be your own kinsman, he perished at the front of the battle for the sake of your pleasure.
Abhimanyu was not protected by us; let him be taken, having laid aside his bow and donned bark garments.
Śakuni: Saubhadra indeed has many protectors; let it be considered that he is surely released. Why?
Because King Virāṭa himself understood that Arjuna’s son would release him.
Or, remembering that he departed from the field of battle today, he might release Dāmodara;
or perhaps Bhīma, fearing Pralamba who brandishes his plow in rage, might set him free;
or else the mighty Bhīma, having slain the powerful enemies, might bring him here.
Droṇa:
Charioteer! Tell me, tell me! How has he been captured now?
Has his chariot overturned, or have the horses bolted, or is the earth unable to bear the wheels and axles?
If his quivers are empty of arrows, if his bowstring is broken and his bow rendered useless,
such are the calamities that befall chariot-warriors in battle through the workings of fate;
yet even when he is dragged away by enemies with their shafts, he remains one whose skill is truly under his own control.
Sūta:
O long-lived one! Man is the embodiment of the science of archery (dhanurveda). Is this not known to you, long-lived one?
Nor have any faults been spoken by you.
And that great chariot, consisting of a flood of arrows,
appeared like a whirling circle of fire; yet my chariot was already seized by that foot-soldier as he rushed forward.
Everyone:
How so? As a footman?
Droṇa: [He is.]
Now, what was that foot-soldier like?
The charioteer replied: "Shall I describe his form or his prowess?"
Bhīṣma:
Women are described by their beauty, but men by their prowess. Therefore, let his prowess be recounted.
Sūta:
Venerable one!
Duryodhana asks: For what reason is someone being praised by you with such arrogant words?
"Let it be told; I have no fear even if this wind [should match] me in speed."
Sūta: Your Majesty ought to listen.
For indeed, having overtaken the horses with speed, he placed his hand upon the chariot-fender.
With Hayagrīva extended forward, the chariot stood motionless.
Bhīṣma: Therefore, let all weapons be laid down. All: [So be it].
For what purpose?
Bhīṣma said:
"If the chariot's speed has been taken away by my arm..."
Let him be considered as one already held in the lap of Vṛkodara;
for in the past, while abducting the daughter of Drupada, Jayadratha was defeated on foot by him alone.
Droṇa:

The son of Gaṅgā has spoken rightly. From the time of his childhood instruction, I have known his speed. Indeed, in the archery hall, when he released an arrow, his head was seen to quiver; this was remarked by me.
Having gone there, he then caught that arrow with his hand as it was equal to a shaft, before it had reached its mark. || 12 ||
Śakuni:
Oh, what a laughable statement! Sir, let me ask you this:
is it not said that there is no one else in the world more powerful than the beloved?
Do you all see the Pāṇḍavas pervading the entire world? || 13 ||
Bhīṣma said:
O King of Gāndhāra! Everything is stated by way of inference.
We shall set out for battle relying upon this.
Armed with weapons and bows, mounted upon their chariots,
Halāyudha and Vṛkodara set forth together for battle, each with only two arms.
Śakuni said:
"We, who are fond of rashness, have been suddenly defeated by Phalguna alone;
moreover, people will speak of that Uttara as being equal to him."
Droṇa:
O King of the Gāndhāras! Even in this matter, you still have doubt.
Is he not also drawn toward the north in battle?
The bow roared as it discharged dry, withered arrows;
was the heat even of the northward sun removed by these shafts, so that the sun set in but a moment? 16.
Bhīṣma:

O son of Gāndhārī! This is indeed being stated quite clearly; surely you understand? By means of words whose syllables are like the feathers of arrows, and which are turned upon the tongue by the wielder of the bow.
Indeed, it was drawn by Pārtha, yet it did not reach his ear. || 17 ||
(Entering) Charioteer:
Victory to Your Majesty! Let the rites for pacification be performed.
Bhīṣma: For what reason?
Sūta:
It was fitting for you to do so previously when your banner was struck by Bāṇa;
for on the feather of this very arrow, someone's name is inscribed. (18)
Bhīṣma: Bring it.
(The charioteer brings it.)
Bhīṣma:
(Taking it and examining it) My child, King of Gāndhāra! My eye is weakened by old age. Let this arrow be described.
Śakuni:
(Taking it up and reciting: "Arjuna's! (With these words he throws it; it falls at Drona's feet.
Drona—(Taking up an arrow: Come, come, my child!
"This arrow, discharged by my disciple to salute Gāṅgeya, has fallen upon the ground at his feet to pay homage to me in due order. (19)
Śakuni: Hold back for a moment, sir! One must now have faith in the evidence of the arrow.
This arrow was released by one who would be a warrior named Arjuna.
And let the written document also be brought forth clearly by Uttara. || 20 ||
Duryodhana said:
"If a falsehood is being uttered for the sake of granting them the kingdom,
I shall give half the kingdom as soon as Yudhiṣṭhira is seen."
(Entering) Attendant: Victory to the Great King! A messenger has arrived from the city of Virāṭa.
Duryodhana:
Let him be admitted.
Soldier: [Does so.]
"As the Great King commands. (Exit) (Then enters Uttara.
Uttara:
My progress along the road has been delayed by the chariot as it travels with horses whose speed is diminished;
for the horses move with difficulty due to the elephants slain by the arrows of the son of Kuntī on all sides, for the ground is indeed uneven.
(Entering with palms joined in reverence) O, O! I salute the entire circle of kings, headed by my preceptor and grandfather.
All:
May you live long!
Droṇa:
What did His Honor, the Lord of Virāṭa, say?
Uttara:
"I have not been sent by His Honor.
Drona: "Then by whom have you been sent?"
Droṇa: By the honorable Yudhiṣṭhira? Uttara: Yes. Droṇa: [Continues]
What did the King of Dharma say?
Uttara replied:
"Listen."
I have obtained Uttara as my daughter-in-law; I await the circle of kings.
Should the wedding take place right there, or here? Where shall it proceed? (23)
Śakuni: Right there, right there! Droṇa: [Right there, right there!]
For this purpose we have been brought here, and even five nights have passed;
since alms were obtained by us in accordance with dharma, let [the gift] be given by dharma alone. (24)
Duryodhana:
Truly, I have granted the kingdom to the Pāṇḍavas exactly as before;
for even when men have died, everyone remains established in truth.
Droṇa:
Ah! We are all delighted, having gathered this great lineage together.
Let this lion among kings rule even this entire earth for us.
(All exit.
The third act.
The Pañcarātra is concluded.
